title: Route policy TTL anomaly - scratch notes
content:
Context:
- Small user-facing outage 2026-02-10 03:12 UTC, traces show increased 5xx during cross-region traffic shift.
- Root surface: smart-routing + route-policy TTL caching interaction?
- This is my personal scratchpad while triaging — not for doc publish yet.

Symptoms observed:
- Sudden jump in token latency and 503s for customers pinned to eu-west1 but routed through eu-central fallback path.
- We saw 'route-eject' events in the routing logs; many requests retried and hit capacity-limited pool in us-east-1.
- TTLs for policy cache entries looked stale (some entries had negative remaining_ttl in logs).

Timeline (quick):
- 02:58 UTC: batch config push to smart-routing policies (small TTL tweak from 60s -> 30s).
- 03:05 UTC: first elevated p50/p95 on eu-west1 (observability alert).
- 03:12 UTC: spike in 5xx and fallback egress to eu-central then to us-east-1.
- 03:40 UTC: rollback routing policy change -> slow recovery.

Immediate checks / commands I ran (notes + outputs paraphrased):
- curl to admin route-config endpoint to fetch live policy for tenant T123:
  curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://routing-api.internal/v1/policies/T123 | jq .
  -> ttl: 30, version: 2026-02-10T02:58Z, fallback: [eu-central, us-east1]

- Live cache introspection on router node rtr-12-euw:
  ssh rtr-12-euw 'sudo /opt/rbin/route-cache inspect --key T123'
  -> cached_entry: policy_v2026-02-09T18:00Z, remaining_ttl: -4  (WTF)

- Queried ringpop/gossip membership for stale entries:
  tcpdump + grep for policy-sync "policy_v2026-02-10" -> saw delayed SYNC events; some nodes didn't accept delta updates due to backpressure.

- Replayed routing decision logs for sample trace id 0x84abc:
  grep 'trace=0x84abc' /var/log/routing/decisions.log | tail -n 50
  -> decision path: match-route -> cache-lookup (miss because remaining_ttl negative) -> default-fallback -> region-eval -> select eu-central -> queue -> reject -> fallback-> us-east1

Error snippets copied from router node: (raw-ish)
- "WARN route-cache: negative ttl for key T123, skipping refresh (age=65234s)"
- "ERROR policy-sync: applyDelta failed: EBUSY backpressure: queue-length 1024"
- "ERROR routing-decision: no healthy endpoints in eu-central pool, ejecting route"

Hypotheses / brain dump (ranked):
1) Cache TTL underflow bug: when config update happens quickly, delta-apply code subtracts previous TTL incorrectly (off-by-one math when clocks skew), producing large negative remaining_ttl. That makes nodes treat entry as expired but with stale policy version id, so fallback picks older fallback lists.
2) Policy-sync backpressure: policy delta apply failing intermittently due to a throughput cap; some nodes never see the new policy, ending up with mixed versions -> route-eject churn.
3) Circuit breaker interplay: route-eject threshold tightened in same release; nodes with stale policy still enforce new tighter thresholds causing mass ejection.
4) Misordered writes: control-plane wrote policy manifest then partially updated central cache; nodes pulling via gossip got inconsistent ordering.

Notes on reproducibility attempts:
- Simulated rolling update in staging with TTL change + induced 200ms clock skew on half the router pool -> observed negative ttl in ~3/40 nodes. Steps:
  1) start policy v1 with ttl 60s
  2) push v2 with ttl 30s concurrently to two controllers
  3) desync clocks on nodes 15-30 by +220ms
  4) run policy-delta apply flood (n=1000) -> some nodes log negative ttl

- Instrumented: added temporary logging to policy-apply code to print pre-apply ttl and delta calc. Observed numeric underflow when delta timestamp older than node's last apply_ts (weird sequence).

Quick patch idea (hotfix):
- Defensive guard: when computed remaining_ttl < 0 and abs(remaining_ttl) < 3600, clamp to 0 (treat as expired) but force immediate fetch of canonical policy instead of skipping refresh. This avoids leaving stale version in cache.
- Also add metrics: policy_delta_apply_fail_count, policy_cache_negative_ttl_count.

Tradeoffs:
- Clamping hides root clock skew issue but reduces blast radius quickly. Need to pair with policy sync hardening.
- Fetching canonical policy aggressively increases control-plane load for brief period — acceptable during incident window.

Follow-ups (owner assignments tentative):
- Asha: roll hotfix to canary router pool and monitor negative_ttl metric (today).
- Marcus: investigate policy-sync backpressure (queue config, EBUSY root cause) - JIRA INFRA-3321.
- Grace: check circuit-breaker thresholds rollout PR and correlation with policy version (GH-PR-4872).

Data to collect for postmortem:
- Full decision traces for 03:00-04:00 UTC for affected tenants.
- Router node state dump for nodes with negative_ttl.
- Control plane write logs around 02:55-03:05 UTC (manifest write order, ack list).
- Network partition / high-latency events from cloud provider during that window.

Questions I still have:
- Why did some nodes compute negative TTL while others didn't? (likely clock skew + race)
- Was there any maintenance or autoscaling event in eu-west1 that reduced policy-sync capacity?
- Are fallback lists computed deterministically from policy OR from a separate region-health snapshot?

Quick checklist for the morning after (if I don't sleep):
- [ ] Canary deploy clamp-hotfix to 5% of routers (rtr-*-canary).
- [ ] Add metric alarm for policy_cache_negative_ttl_count > 1 in 5m.
- [ ] Run targeted re-sync to all routers for tenant T123.
- [ ] Postmortem draft skeleton (include timeline + root cause hypothesis + remediation + RCC).

Misc scribbles / CLI snippets for others: (paste into slack thread)
- inspect cache on node: ssh $NODE 'sudo /opt/rbin/route-cache inspect --json --key $TENANT'
- force fetch: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://routing-api.internal/v1/policies/$TENANT/force-refresh
- show apply failures: kubectl -n routing logs deploy/policy-controller | grep 'applyDelta' | tail -n 200

Closing note:
- This felt like a confluence of small race conditions (TTL arithmetic, policy-sync backlog, tightened eject thresholds) rather than a single catastrophic bug. Immediate mitigations should prioritize minimizing mixed-policy states across router pool.

- Tagging Marcus + Grace in thread for visibility.

-- Asha
